transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess I’m here because I keep getting stuck on work that takes real focus… sitting down with monthly reports, or planning bigger health events across sites. I know it matters, but it’s like I hit a wall and put it off.
Did you have similar trouble focusing or finishing tasks when you were a child?

Yeah… I think so. In elementary school, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but I was always kind of daydreaming. I’d lose worksheets or forget to turn in homework unless my mom went through my backpack every night.
Do you also have this kind of trouble staying organized or following through with tasks at home?

Yeah… it shows up at home too. When I’m juggling work projects, committee stuff, outreach events… I’ll have notes in a few different places, and I can’t really sort out what needs to happen first. Then I end up rushing at the end.
Outside of work and home, do you also have this same kind of trouble staying organized or following through in other parts of your life?

Yeah… some. With the memorial committee and outreach events, it’s similar. I’ll have notes scattered in a few places, and then I kind of freeze on what should come first. So I end up scrambling near the end.
Do you often make careless mistakes because your attention drifts, even when you understand the task?

Yeah… that happens. I’ll send out a clinic staffing schedule or even a soccer league email thinking I looked it over, and then someone points out I had the wrong date or left off the location. Stuff I really should’ve caught.
When you were in school, did you often have trouble paying attention in class?

Yeah… I think so. Even back in elementary school, teachers would tell my parents I was bright, but I’d be staring off, losing worksheets, forgetting homework. My mom had to check my backpack most nights or it just wouldn’t get turned in.
Do you often find yourself worrying a lot about many different things?
I don’t know… not really “many different things,” I guess. I worry some, like anyone, but I haven’t noticed it being the main issue.
Did these problems get noticeably worse after a specific stressful life event?

Yeah… I’d say it became more noticeable after my friend died. That was almost two years ago, and I ended up taking on more with the league and outreach stuff after that. Since then it’s been harder to keep up.
When you’re doing something that requires steady mental effort, do you often find your attention drifting even when you want to stay focused?

Yeah. That’s honestly the main thing that made me come in. If it’s something that takes real sit-down brain work—monthly reports, or planning a bigger health event across sites—I just… hit a wall. I’ll want to do it, I know it matters, but my attention drifts and I keep putting it off.
Before your friend died, were these focus and organization problems already causing significant problems for you as an adult?

Not really significant, no. It’s been more like… since my friend died, almost two years ago. About a year and eleven months. After I took on more with the league and outreach, that’s when it started causing real problems.
Since your friend died, have these concentration and organization problems felt mainly tied to that loss?
I’m not sure. I mean, it lines up with that period, but I don’t know if it’s mainly the loss itself or just… everything that came after. I haven’t really sorted that out.
Do you still find yourself preoccupied with thoughts of your friend’s death?
I don’t know. I think about him sometimes, yeah, but I’m not sure I’d call it preoccupied. It’s… hard to say.
When your focus falls apart, is it usually because your mind goes back to your friend or the loss?
I don’t really know. Sometimes I guess it could, but I haven’t noticed it being that specific. It’s more like my mind just… goes somewhere else, and I lose the thread.
Do reminders of your friend’s death tend to bring on the focus problems?
I haven’t really noticed a clear connection. Reminders can affect me, I guess, but I can’t say that’s what usually sets off the focus problems.
Before your friend died, were these focus and organization problems already causing significant problems for you in any part of your adult life?

Not really. I mean, I had my moments before, but it wasn’t causing major problems. It’s been more like the last almost two years… since my friend died and I took on more of the league and outreach stuff.
Before your friend died, were these attention and organization problems causing major trouble at work?
No, not really major trouble before then. It’s mostly been these last… almost two years, since my friend died and I ended up taking on more with the league and outreach stuff.
Since your friend died, have you been feeling down or depressed much of the time?
I don’t know… not much of the time, I wouldn’t say. I’ve had rough days, sure, but I’m not sure I’d call it depressed most of the time.
Do these concentration and organization problems feel mainly caused by the stress of everything that changed after your friend died?
Yeah… I guess it lines up with that. It’s been going on about a year and eleven months, since my friend died and I took on more of the league and outreach responsibilities.
Even during calmer periods of your adult life, did you still have the same trouble with attention and organization?
I mean… not really the same. It’s mostly been going on since my friend died, about a year and eleven months ago, when I took on more with the league and outreach stuff.
Do these problems make it hard for you to keep up with the extra responsibilities you took on after your friend died?

Yeah… it does. I’m still managing, mostly, but not cleanly. People have had to pick up after me here and there, and some deadlines have slipped. I’ve had to send a few last-minute apology messages to coworkers or friends, which… yeah, that’s embarrassing.
